purpose: Research direction: geodesic intelligence. DSV4 communicates; ECS/EDEN computes, learns and persists; FMS materializes; HACF/structure organizes persistent structural memory; continuity binds the minimal durable runtime lineage/authority (docs/ELPIS_MISSION.md). Computation is meant to happen in a persistent, evolving ECS substrate, entered and left through the DSV4 token boundary, not in a transformer. This is an architectural research direction, not a claim of general intelligence.

division: ECS / EDEN computes, learns and persists.
HACF / structure organizes persistent structural memory.

mission.canonical_dataflow: text -> DSV4 encode -> admitted ECS stimulus -> ECS/EDEN dynamics -> ECS readout -> DSV4 decode -> text (runtime.cognition.run_turn)
mission.prohibited: ECS as a sidecar around a full DSV model: ECS state conditioning a DSV model, or ECS driven by a DSV model's output statistics (forensic: f4e1f05, 75313fb).

subsystems.purpose: Machine/OS substrate, resource authority and materialization for Elpis: content hashing, FMS residency (HOT/WARM/COLD logical tiers over RAM/device/storage physical domains) with a POSIX platform abstraction layer, Linux descriptor capabilities, sealed native loading, deployment-pinned resource authority and verified file-backed assets materialized on demand into bounded residency; plus the vendor-neutral bounded native execution scheduler and explicit post-compiled accelerator backend port. Its constitutional invariant is persistent logical capacity >= resident materialization >= actively executing materialization; its generic core names no DSV-specific tensor role (mission-gated).
subsystems.mutation_authority: The substrate never mutates admitted external assets (no writable replicas). It owns only its own residency state: page registration, leases and eviction inside configured budgets. Admission requires a deployment-pinned catalog; inspection never creates authority.

subsystems.security_boundary: Trusted root selected once; opens resolve beneath its descriptor with openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS; native code is copied into a sealed memfd, digest-verified, then loaded. Linux only; other platforms fail closed.

subsystems.purpose: The one canonical ECS: the ECS/EDEN-facing cognitive/dynamical substrate of Elpis. It owns authoritative microscopic state W, exact cubic forward/S3 mathematics (S3 is a derived coarse observable), deterministic atomic microscopic recurrence, epoch tracking and deterministic portable snapshot/restore. A native executor (ecsg_executor.h, docs/ECS_RUNTIME_R1.md) is the runtime form of the state: one-call query, one-call fused K-step learn, native candidate transactions committed by pointer exchange with generation staleness, SINGLE_WRITER enforced, no allocation after creation, bitwise equal to the scalar reference. A stdlib-only Python binding (elpis.ECS.native) controls it over a caller-loaded library (Executor, Transaction; WorldState is the scalar reference binding). Cognitive R0 (elpis.ECS.cognition.CognitiveCore) keeps QUERY (x -> f_W(x) from the current W, read-only, one native call) distinct from LEARN ((X, y) -> K G1 steps in one native call -> one native commit). ECS imports no inference, codec, runtime or continuity module. Mutable FMS R0 is an additive residency adapter: authoritative idle ECS snapshots are generic FMS objects, while execution restores the unchanged qualified Runtime R1 executor through its public ABI. Native K1 is the canonical retained-state runtime under the ecsg-k1-native.v2 QUALIFIED authority, with complete authoritative state (W, epoch, H, a), native learning/consolidation, complete-state transactions and generic FMS residency.
subsystems.mutation_authority: Only ECS cognitive state changes through the qualified cubic full-batch gradient step. Existing Runtime R1 executor semantics remain unchanged. In Mutable FMS R0 an FMS object owns the complete portable W+epoch snapshot between operations; ECS computes a complete candidate and publishes a complete replacement only on successful commit. QUERY never mutates cognitive state. FMS may mutate only its own residency and verified cold-replica state; it never decides learning semantics. No continuity, HACF, inference or canonical state is mutated by ECS.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition's canonical turn (elpis.runtime.cognition.run_turn) places ECS between DSV4 encode and DSV4 decode over a native K1 state (K1State, or the FMS-resident K1FMSState). An admitted stimulus enters only as a native-ready ordered experience schedule (contiguous X and y, and (rows, steps) descriptors); one native K1 call learns and consolidates every experience on a transaction candidate of (W, epoch, H, a) and returns S3 of the candidate W, the readout handed to the decode boundary; the complete K1 candidate is committed natively only when the whole turn succeeds. ECS is never a conditioning input to, or driven by, a DSV model. The Runtime R1 Executor remains a qualified primitive and the K1-disabled reference, but it is not the substrate of the canonical turn. The FMS-resident K1 path runs the same turn over the resident bytes, with no per-turn restore or serialization.
subsystems.security_boundary: The qualified Runtime R1 executor remains SINGLE_WRITER and retains its existing allocation, validation and callback rules. Mutable FMS R0 adds numeric logical-state handles, an exclusive per-state guard and generic FMS leases. No raw FMS pointer escapes the native adapter. A direct operation restores a transient executor while the lease is held; an open transaction retains one executor and one WRITE lease until commit or abort. ECS itself performs no path discovery; POSIX cold storage is owned by the substrate FMS/PAL capability supplied by the caller.

subsystems.purpose: Continuity records the current durable lineage/authority needed for safe restart: the expected K1 retained-state identity of the ECS lineage (explicitly anchored, advanced only by committed turns) and the current head of admitted evolution path transitions plus one pending assertion identity. One fixed-size 176-byte record in a two-slot crash-safe register (docs/CONTINUITY.md). The authority is implemented in Rust (native/continuity) behind a stable C ABI (include/elpis/continuity.h); elpis.continuity is a thin Python adapter over that ABI and owns no format, transition law or digest. It is not an ECS, not context memory, not an event history, not topology, not a message bus and not an audit ledger.
subsystems.mutation_authority: The Rust store (elpis_continuity_*): anchor_cognition (once, explicit), commit_cognition (only from the current expected K1 identity), reserve_evolution (idle to pending before execution) and finalize_evolution (only from the exact current pending authority to the next idle revision). Each publishes one complete next record into the non-current slot and fdatasyncs it; nothing else writes the directory.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composes it: one store per Runtime. The canonical K1 turn publishes the new expected K1 identity after the one native K1 commit; evolution validates, durably reserves its assertion, executes once, and finalizes pending authority.
subsystems.persistence: Exactly two fixed 176-byte slot files; the valid record with the higher generation is the authority. Constant storage (352 bytes), constant restart work (two reads) and constant resident memory. No log, no replay, no compaction, no retained history.

subsystems.purpose: Two paths. (1) Bounded ingress: a streaming Regex lexer over a bounded interval-specification grammar -> read-only HACF lexical retrieval and one-hop context graph -> a zero-authority context proposal -> an atomic query-local proposal batch published as a semantic query overlay; ambiguity rejects before any batch. (2) The canonical Grid81 writer pipeline, one authority boundary per stage: deterministic structural adjudication -> capability authority decision and one granted-unconsumed structural-influence capability -> capability consumption into an inert artifact -> application against shadow capability state with a durable SQLite application ledger -> read-only advisory promotion plan -> promotion authority (explicit operator approval, one-use capability) -> isolated successor candidate -> atomic publication (durable publication ledger reservation, renameat2 exchange, post-commit verification through the canonical reader).
subsystems.mutation_authority: Ingress mutates nothing: it opens an existing HACF corpus, performs only lexical reads and never creates one, and every result carries zero semantic, admission, execution and runtime authority. Only elpis.pipeline.canonical.publisher changes canonical Grid81 state, and only with the exact one-use promotion capability object issued by elpis.pipeline.canonical.authority against an explicit operator approval digest. Adjudication, capability evaluation and promotion planning are read-only; consumption and application write only caller-owned shadow state and ledgers.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition may run ingress on caller-supplied bytes against a corpus it owns; its edge adapters turn the proposal export into object claims and address proposals for structural-memory rendering. It may drive the writer stages in process. Nothing runs implicitly, and each stage consumes only the previous stage's typed output.
subsystems.security_boundary: Ingress takes bytes, never paths to read; the bounded lexer refuses input beyond its carry profile before any evidence is built; the bridge library is loaded only from an explicit path, exports only its declared ABI (linker version script) and refuses symlinked, relative or absent corpus roots. The Python binding re-reads the four authority flags and refuses any result that claims authority. Fail closed at every stage: proposals and model output are never authority; the promotion plan is advisory and non-executable; the one-use promotion capability binds the source canonical digest and generation it was issued against, and the publisher re-reads the canonical root under an exclusive flock on its Canonical parent and refuses any other state, symlinked layout, or candidate inside the root; publication reserves a durable ledger entry, exchanges atomically with renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) and verifies through the production reader; replay is idempotent and a consumed capability cannot be reused. Linux only.

subsystems.purpose: Generic, deterministic evolution: canonical integer genotypes, bounded mutation seeded from content-addressed lineage, persistent organisms with a lifecycle law, atomic energy-conserving reproduction, exact integer fitness, self-verified truncation selection over a population revision, an evolution path gate that admits one bounded attempt per exact ECS-history-bound assertion and chains transition receipts, and evaluation-gated promotion of a candidate workspace over its incumbent with atomic materialization.
subsystems.mutation_authority: Evolution records are immutable values; every state change returns a new population, organism or receipt and nothing is written in place. Selection and reproduction commit only against the exact revision the caller observed and reject atomically otherwise. Promotion writes a child workspace only at a caller-supplied, not-yet-existing destination, and only when its content matches the selected manifest. The path gate grants no authority beyond the single attempt it admits.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition may run gated evolution attempts bound to the current evolution authority held by continuity; an admitted attempt advances that authority to its transition receipt digest, so a stale assertion executes nothing.
subsystems.security_boundary: No implicit randomness (mutation seeds derive from lineage content), no model, no numerics, no network. Selection accepts no externally proposed solution and recomputes every fitness score. The path gate type-checks the supplied evolution authority binding and executes nothing for a rejected or retired-schema assertion. Promotion refuses symlinks and special files in workspaces and edit paths outside the child.

subsystems.purpose: The DSV4 communication codec: the token boundary between human/token space and the ECS substrate, never cognition. Canonical codec modules: text (digest-bound DeepSeek recipe V4.1 tokenizer, chat/text rendering and incremental decoding with at most three carry bytes), contracts, admission and structural (budgeted, frozen token rendering of verified structural-memory objects). Everything else in elpis.inference is noncanonical DSV model-execution mechanics retained for historical replay of persisted identities and for qualification: the legacy compact DSV4 synthetic target, the atomic decode transaction, the sequence and principal paths, steering, speculative drafting, associative rows, experts, prefetch, global context and read-only safetensors preflight. The runtime never composes them (mission-gated). The production-shaped DSV4.1 tower is not here: it lives in research/dsv41_tower.
subsystems.mutation_authority: The codec mutates nothing: it encodes, decodes and renders. It owns no ECS state and imports no ECS, continuity or runtime module (boundary- and mission-gated). The retained model-execution mechanics commit only their own decode/sequence state against an exact expected state; every proposal record is ProposalOnly with zero authority, and model output is never authority.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime uses only the codec modules: the tokenizer's encode/decode at the canonical turn's token boundary and budgeted rendering of admitted structural memory. It runs no DSV model.
subsystems.security_boundary: No network, no downloads and no implicit model: a target exists only from caller-supplied, digest-verified file assets registered through elpis.substrate beneath its trusted root, and every bank, expert, parameter artifact and projection is bound to the target's model identity. Prefetch predicts physical ranges only and cannot change which rows are read. Proposals arrive as already validated, digest-pinned AddressProposal values and are checked against the snapshot they are bound to. elpis.inference imports no ECS, structure, pipeline, evolution or runtime module, directly or transitively (boundary-tested). Fixed IEEE-754 binary64 arithmetic in steering; no hidden or global mutable recurrence state.

subsystems.purpose: The one runtime composition. Its mutable systems authority (lifecycle, fail-stop, the embedded continuity store, the K1 lineage binding, the managed turn's native K1 transaction and its continuity publication, and the evolution reservation) is RuntimeCore (native/runtime, Rust, C ABI include/elpis/runtime.h; docs/RUNTIME_CORE.md); elpis.runtime.Runtime is its thin facade. It orchestrates codec -> ECS -> codec (elpis.runtime.cognition.run_turn: DSV4 encode, admitted stimulus, ECS dynamics, S3 readout, DSV4 decode), failing closed with ECS_CODEC_UNQUALIFIED while no qualified ECS codec map exists. It composes the one ECS and the continuity component: the first managed K1 lineage is anchored explicitly, every committed turn publishes its new expected K1 retained-state identity, and evolution attempts are bound to the current evolution authority. It runs one subsystem operation at a time through that subsystem's own fail-closed entry point (pipeline ingress, structure retrieval-bundle admission, canonical Grid81 publication, the evolution path gate, and structural-memory rendering through the codec) and returns that subsystem's result; it keeps no receipts and no history. It owns the edge adapters (elpis.runtime.edges). It composes no DSV model execution: no decode transaction, principal sequence or model text generation (mission-gated). It is not a numbered runtime generation.
subsystems.mutation_authority: RuntimeCore (native/runtime) writes only the continuity directory, through the embedded continuity store: the explicit K1 lineage anchor, the expected K1 identity after each committed K1 turn, and the evolution authority (reservation, then finalization) around each admitted attempt. A failed or uncertain continuity publication never rolls back a committed K1 turn; it fail-stops RuntimeCore until reopen. The Python facade holds no authority state. Every other state change (canonical publication and its ledger, decode state, evolution receipts) is made by the owning subsystem's entry point with the caller's explicit inputs; the runtime adds no authority, no fallback and no audit record.
subsystems.security_boundary: The continuity directory is an explicit absolute path owned exclusively (directory flock); its two fixed slots are verified on open and a corrupt, ambiguous, foreign or retired receipt-history layout is refused. A supplied K1 state whose retained-state identity differs from the durable expectation is refused before any K1 mutation (CONTINUITY_STATE_MISMATCH); there is no implicit anchor and no synthesized transition. Libraries, corpus roots, file assets, ledgers and promotion capabilities are supplied explicitly by the caller; the runtime opens no network connection and loads no model. An evolution assertion built against an older evolution authority is rejected before anything executes.
protocol_identifiers_retained: None of its own: the runtime builds on elpis.continuity.register.v2 and elpis.continuity.evolution-authority.v2 (owned by continuity) and the ECS ABI.
subsystems.model_dependency: NONE_REQUIRED. Inference runs only on caller-supplied targets; the integration suite uses the synthetic DSV4 fixture.
subsystems.maturity: Integration qualified over real native libraries and a real HACF corpus (ingress, structural memory, canonical writer, evolution, structural-memory rendering), including continuity untouched by subsystem operations, explicit K1 anchor, matched restart, mismatched restart refused before K1 mutation, K1 commit with failed continuity publication kept and fail-stopped, evolution stale-authority rejection across restart, and legacy receipt-history refusal. The canonical turn is qualified for direction, atomicity, determinism, snapshot continuation, fail-closed refusal and the absence of any DSV model, using TRAINING=NONE SEMANTICS=NONE interface fixtures only.
incomplete_interfaces: No qualified ECS<->DSV semantic codec map exists; canonical text generation is unavailable by design.
No HACF/structure -> ECS edge is defined; Runtime.admit_context renders structural memory through the codec but nothing canonical consumes the rendering yet.
The query-local ingress overlay is not persisted; it lives in the returned ingress result only.
The runtime is single-process; no cross-process transport or service boundary.
No audit trail of runtime operations is kept (by design): ingress, retrieval, publication and admission results are returned, not recorded.
